title.narrative: Provision of life-saving child protection and gender-based violence interventions for vulnerable populations at risk during the lean season in Borno

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project will address the specialized needs and gaps in child protection and gender-based violence across the conflict-affected local government areas of Dikwa and Ngala LGAs in Borno State, Northeastern Nigeria. It will build on completed Protection and Education in emergency projects in areas where Street Child has a long-established presence. Through coordinating with our local partners Protection without Borders League (POWIB) will deliver an integrated, holistic set of activities that draw on our collective strengths in Child Protection and Gender Based Violence programming while Cedar Foundation for Disability (CFfD), with deliver disability inclusion and Protection Mainstreaming based technical expertise and experience in delivery similar programming in the past with through our collective efforts and holistic value additionltbrgtStreet Child, POWIB and CFID are all experienced partner with good experience working across the Northeast on Child Protection and GBV projects and together have implemented the lean season 1st reserve allocation in 2023 in same proposed locations of Dikwa and Ngala LGA of Borno State and with CFID, together we implemented the disability consortium project in Bama and MMC. ltbrgtDrawing on our long experience managing the consortium, Street Child will provide oversight and capacity-building support to our partners, while offering a range of feedback mechanisms to ensure that all our work is accountable to the local population. The partnership will work out of the same facilities and communities to ensure we benefit from regular contact through cross referrals, complementing with other partners, service provision and tracked progress whilst easing the time and cost of referrals. Street Child will also run training with staff, partners and locally contracted volunteers on a range this in informed based on our documented lesson learned from previous NHF funded projects on the 1st reserve allocation NGO consortium in 2023 and 2024. ltbrgtIn addition to our coordination role, Street Child will provide specialized services to complement our partners’ activities. Through responding to our partners’ case management referrals, we will provide cash support to high-risk beneficiaries, Family Tracing and Reunification (FTR) services to unaccompanied children including the provision of alternative care facilities or transport to reunify displaced family members. Parenting programmes to foster carers or other caregivers will be built on and rolled out to new attendees of our nutrition partner’s work. Children identified at risk including GBV survivors through our partners Psychosocial Support and life skills training will be referred to our Mental Health Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) specialist who can provide support, counselling and dedicated psychological assistance including referrals for tier 4 services.ltbrgtTo ensure our partners’ case management services provided are comprehensive, referral pathways will be mapped out (if not already available) and strengthened through advocacy and coordination with the relevant clusters at the community and LGA level. ltbrgtFinally, Street Child will use their experience of building the technical and organizational capacity of local partners to develop a strong capacity support plan. This will involve mainstreaming protection issues through training on PSEA, GBV, Disability inclusion, and child safeguarding, developing responsive monitoring activities that encourage active participation from our attendees, and creating shared CRM systems that hold us accountable to the local population. Through the involvement of government authority across the Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development, Primary health care, and the Ministry of Health representatives and social workers in all trainings and field activities will also promote government buy-in and strengthen government capacity on ownership and sustainability.ltbrgtlt/pgt
